angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 32,238,738 km at 100.91 pc = 4.27 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 46750: distance 100.908 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.018), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 100.908 +/- 1.816 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 8.7555 +/- 0.1890 mas (same row, RUWE 1.12), 46.3 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 46.34 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 46750: radius 46.34 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 454.175 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.066) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 32,238,738 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 3917 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 46750: effective temperature 3917 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.113) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 46750: effective temperature 3917 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.113) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * lam Leo: spectral type K4.5III (1989ApJS...71..245K)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * lam Leo: main object type *, Star
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * lam Leo: projected rotation speed 2.9 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2005yCat.3244....0G)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 542) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 1.3 from 2007A&A...475.1003H; the 7 published values span log g 1.3 to 1.6, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2007A%26A...475.1003H)
